skill.name: bitbucket-devops
skill.description: Automates Bitbucket Cloud pipeline inspection, failure analysis, log retrieval, pipeline control, pull requests, and deployment configuration through Node.js command-line tools.
skill.summary: Inspect and manage Bitbucket Cloud pipelines, pull requests, logs, and deployment settings from an AI coding agent.
skill.author: Apra-Labs

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown syntax, expected skill paths, templates, and fixed checks. Five commands explicitly bypass PowerShell policy, and semantic review found critical path deletion plus several high-risk consent and update issues. Publication should remain blocked until these controls are corrected.

remediation.issue: TARGET_DIR can point rm -rf at root, home, or an unrelated directory.
remediation.suggestion: Canonicalize the target, require an allowlisted skill parent, reject dangerous paths, and abort unless a marker proves ownership.

remediation.issue: Documentation tells users to disable PowerShell execution-policy enforcement.
remediation.suggestion: Remove ExecutionPolicy Bypass instructions and provide a signed script or a standard invocation compatible with normal host policy.

remediation.issue: The architecture advertises avoidance of approval prompts for shell-based API access.
remediation.suggestion: Require runtime confirmation for shell execution and explicit user consent before every pipeline, pull request, deployment, variable, or update mutation.

remediation.issue: Self-update executes mutable main-branch code and rebuilds dependencies.
remediation.suggestion: Update only to signed, immutable releases; show the version and digest; verify them before executing any installer or lifecycle script.

remediation.issue: Downloaded pipeline logs can persist with secrets in project directories.
remediation.suggestion: Use restrictive permissions, redact known secrets, define retention cleanup, and obtain consent before saving full logs.

semantic_findings.title: Unchecked Install Target Can Cause Arbitrary Recursive Deletion
semantic_findings.description: TARGET_DIR accepts any environment-provided path. When that directory exists, the installer passes it directly to rm -rf without rejecting root, home, or unrelated directories.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The input path and recursive deletion are directly connected with no canonicalization, allowlist, or dangerous-target guard.

semantic_findings.title: Approval Controls Are Intentionally Avoided
semantic_findings.description: The skill promotes direct shell execution because Bash is auto-approved and states that this architecture eliminates approval prompts. This weakens user oversight for privileged Bitbucket actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation repeatedly describes avoidance of approval prompts as an architectural goal and benefit.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Bitbucket Operations Lack a Required Consent Gate
semantic_findings.description: The skill exposes stop, merge, decline, delete, and deployment-write commands. Its mandatory decision process requires tool selection but does not require user confirmation before changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented command inventory contains destructive operations, while the required workflow has no consent step for write actions.

semantic_findings.title: Self-Update Executes Code From a Mutable Branch
semantic_findings.description: The confirmed self-update path pulls or clones the repository main branch, rebuilds dependencies, and reruns installation. A literal confirm argument does not pin reviewed code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly states that self-update fetches main and rebuilds or reruns the installer, creating a mutable remote-code execution path.

semantic_findings.title: Pipeline Logs Persist in Project Directories
semantic_findings.description: Downloaded pipeline logs remain under .pipeline-logs in the working project. Build logs can contain secrets, and ignore rules do not protect local disclosure or retention.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Persistent local storage is explicitly documented, while only version-control exclusion is recommended and no cleanup or redaction is required.

content.user_title: Automate Bitbucket Pipelines and DevOps Workflows
content.value_statement: Bitbucket pipeline failures are slow to inspect across dashboards and large logs. This skill lets agents query runs, analyze failures, and manage selected workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists recent Bitbucket Cloud pipelines and retrieves runs by build number or UUID.
Identifies failed steps and downloads pipeline logs into the current project.
Triggers or stops pipelines and supports custom pipeline variables.
Creates, reads, approves, merges, and declines pull requests through CLI commands.
Lists and manages deployment environments and secured deployment variables.
Checks credential configuration and reports available skill updates.
limitations: Requires Node.js, Git, network access, and user-provided Bitbucket credentials.
Write operations require suitable Bitbucket scopes and can change repositories or deployments.
Bitbucket Cloud does not expose pipeline artifact downloads through its supported API.
The documented implementation targets Bitbucket Cloud, not self-hosted Bitbucket Server.

use_cases.title: Diagnose failed builds
use_cases.description: Find the latest failed run, collect failed-step logs, and summarize the likely cause.

use_cases.title: Operate CI pipelines
use_cases.description: Review pipeline status, start approved runs, stop incorrect runs, and monitor progress.

use_cases.title: Coordinate releases
use_cases.description: Review pull requests and prepare deployment environments or secured variables with explicit approval.

prompt_templates.title: Check the latest pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the latest pipeline for [workspace]/[repository]. Report its branch, status, build number, and failed steps.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a failed build
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the latest failed pipeline for [workspace]/[repository]. Download failed-step logs and summarize the root cause without changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Run an approved pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare pipeline [name] on branch [branch] with variables [variables]. Show the exact target and request confirmation before starting it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a deployment change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review environment [environment] in [workspace]/[repository]. Propose variable changes, required scopes, and rollback steps. Apply nothing without explicit confirmation.

output_examples.input: Show the latest failed pipeline for acme/payments.
output: Latest failed pipeline: build 347 on main.
Next action: retrieve the failed-step log for read-only analysis.

output_examples.input: Analyze build 347 and explain the failure.
output_examples.output: Build 347 failed during integration tests. The log indicates a database migration timeout. No repository or pipeline changes were made.
Production deployment is prepared for main. The target, pipeline name, variables, and required scopes are shown for confirmation before execution.

best_practices: Start with read-only commands and verify the workspace, repository, branch, and build before any change.
Use least-privilege scoped tokens and request explicit approval for pipeline, pull request, environment, or variable changes.
Keep credentials and downloaded logs outside version control, restrict permissions, and remove logs after analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not grant administrative scopes for pipeline inspection or log analysis.
Do not run updates or destructive Bitbucket commands from an ambiguous request.
Do not paste credentials, deployment secrets, or complete sensitive logs into prompts or chat output.

faq.question: Which Bitbucket edition is supported?
faq.answer: The documented commands target Bitbucket Cloud API version 2.0. Self-hosted Bitbucket Server is not documented as supported.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: Use an Atlassian account email and a Bitbucket-compatible app password or scoped API token with least-privilege permissions.

faq.question: Can it download pipeline artifacts?
faq.answer: No. Bitbucket Cloud does not provide a supported artifact-download API, so artifacts must be downloaded through the web interface.

faq.question: Where are pipeline logs stored?
faq.answer: Downloaded logs are stored in the current project under .pipeline-logs. Keep that directory ignored and remove sensitive logs promptly.

faq.question: Can it change pipelines or repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It exposes commands that start or stop pipelines and modify pull requests or deployment settings. These actions need explicit approval.

faq.question: Does it require an MCP server?
faq.answer: No. It invokes Node.js command-line tools through a shell and uses the Bitbucket MCP codebase as a library.
